findings.title: updateDevice uses ? placeholders incompatible with Postgres
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice builds a query with ? placeholders for all databases, while CreateOrUpdateDevice in the same file correctly uses $1..$5 for Postgres. The Postgres driver / xorm Exec will not bind ? placeholders, so the limit-reached update path will fail with a syntax error on Postgres while working on SQLite/MySQL.

findings.title: Check-then-act race allows device limit bypass
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice first does CountDevices and then either updateDevice or INSERT in separate transactions/sessions with no lock or unique constraint enforcement. Concurrent anonymous logins can both observe count < limit and both INSERT, exceeding the configured device_limit. The limit is therefore not reliably enforced under concurrency.

findings.title: Expired devices can never re-register once limit reached
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go: CountDevices counts only devices updated within anonymousDeviceExpiration, but updateDevice also requires WHERE updated_at BETWEEN expiration and now. A returning device whose row expired and was not yet cleaned up will match zero rows and get ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being re-inserted/updated, permanently locking out that device ID even though it should be treated as a new slot after expiration.

findings.title: Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on DB with no timeout
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Authenticate changed TagDevice from a background goroutine with 2-minute timeout and panic recovery to a synchronous call using the request context. Every anonymous authentication now incurs a CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE round-trip on the hot path, adding latency and allowing a slow DB to block/hang login with no timeout, a denial-of-service and performance regression.

findings.title: Local cache poisoned before DB result hides limit error
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI does localCache.SetDefault before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never evicts on error. If the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the device ID stays cached so subsequent TagDevice calls return nil early without touching the DB, turning a rejected device into an apparently successful tag while it was never persisted, making enforcement inconsistent.

findings.title: Provider signature change breaks DI and testability
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed its parameter from anonstore.AnonStore interface to concrete sqlStore db.DB and constructs the store internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. This removes inversion of control, prevents mocking the store in tests/wire, and no wire_gen update is included, so existing dependency-injection wiring that supplies an AnonStore will fail to build.

findings.title: Raw device-limit error returned as auth failure
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Authenticate returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached directly when the limit is hit. Callers of authn.Client expect authentication errors, and returning a raw storage sentinel leaks an internal message and provides no HTTP status / user-facing handling for rejected anonymous devices, likely surfacing as 500 instead of a controlled rejection.

findings.title: untagDevice logs wrong error variable
findings.body: File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go untagDevice logs a.log.Debug("Failed to untag device", "error", err) where err is the post-login hook input parameter, not errD from DeleteDevice. On delete failure it therefore logs nil/the unrelated hook error, hiding the real failure and complicating debugging.
